DSSSB Combined Exam 2026 Selection Process

Separate examinations are held for each post code. Minimum qualifying marks (MCQ/Descriptive stages): UR/EWS – 50%, OBC(Delhi)/SC/ST/PwBD/ESM – 45%. Each MCQ carries 1 mark, with negative marking of 0.25 for each wrong answer.

Senior Personal Assistant & Personal Assistant (Post Code 805/26)

Tier Format Marks / Detail
Tier-I MCQ (shortlisting) 90 marks, 90 min – English & Comprehension (50), GK (20), General Intelligence (20); up to 25× vacancies shortlisted
Tier-II Descriptive (English) 75 marks, 90 min – Essay 250 words (30), Grammar (25), Translation 20 words (20); up to 10× vacancies shortlisted for skill test
Tier-III Skill Test (qualifying) Senior PA: 550-word dictation (5 min) + 40-min transcription, max 22 errors (4%). PA: 500-word dictation + 40-min transcription, max 20 errors (4%). Typing @ 40 wpm for both.
Tier-IV Interview 10 marks, no minimum qualifying marks; conducted by Delhi District Courts; final merit on Tier-II + Tier-IV combined

Junior Judicial Assistant (Post Code 806/26)

Tier Format Marks / Detail
Tier-I MCQ (shortlisting) 120 marks, 120 min – English & Comprehension (60), GK (30), General Intelligence (30); up to 25× vacancies shortlisted
Tier-II Descriptive (English) 100 marks, 120 min – Essay 300 words (50), Grammar (30), Translation 25 words (20); up to 10× vacancies shortlisted for skill test
Tier-III Skill Test (qualifying) Typing test @ 40 wpm
Tier-IV Interview 15 marks, no minimum qualifying marks; final merit on Tier-II + Tier-IV combined

Process Server (Post Code 807/26)

Tier Format Marks / Detail
Tier-I Objective/MCQ (Bilingual, Eng+Hindi) 100 marks, 120 min (160 min for PwBD) – English (25), Hindi (25), GK (25), Arithmetic (25); up to 15× vacancies shortlisted
Tier-II Driving/Skill Test (qualifying) Conducted in real traffic conditions
Tier-III Interview 15 marks, no minimum qualifying marks; final selection on Tier-I + Tier-III combined

Peon/Orderly/Dak Peon (Post Code 808/26)

Tier Format Marks / Detail
Tier-I Objective/MCQ (Bilingual, Eng+Hindi) 100 marks, 120 min (160 min for PwBD) – English (25), Hindi (25), GK (25), Arithmetic (25); up to 10× vacancies shortlisted for interview
Tier-II Interview 15 marks, no minimum qualifying marks; final selection on Tier-I + Tier-II combined
  • DSSSB conducts the MCQ, Descriptive and Shorthand/Typing tests; Delhi District Courts (Tis Hazari) conducts the Driving Test/Interview and prepares the final merit list
  • Marks from Computer Based Examinations are normalized (where applicable) as per DSSSB's published formula
  • No re-evaluation/re-checking of answer sheets is permitted
  • In a tie, the senior-in-age candidate ranks higher; if DOB also matches, alphabetical order of first name (English) decides

How to Apply for DSSSB Combined Exam 2026

  1. Register (one-time) on dsssbonline.nic.in, if not already registered with DSSSB; this generates a common User ID/Password for all future DSSSB exams.
  2. Log in and apply online for the post(s)/post code(s) of your choice between 06.10.2026 (12:00 Noon) and 04.11.2026 (11:00 PM).
  3. Fill in all details carefully – no correction/modification (including category change) is allowed after final submission.
  4. Upload a recent, clear colour photograph (plain white/off-white background, full face, eyes open) and signature.
  5. Pay the applicable fee, if any, only through SBI e-Pay.
  6. Submit well before the closing date and take a printout of the confirmed application for your records.

Application Fee

Category Fee
UR / OBC / EWS (Male) ₹100
Women (any category) / SC / ST / PwBD / Ex-Servicemen Exempted (Nil)
Important: Ex-servicemen already re-employed on a regular basis in Central/Delhi Govt. civil posts after availing ESM reservation benefits are not eligible for the fee concession. Fee once paid is non-refundable, and only SBI e-Pay is accepted.

Documents Required

  • Matriculation/Secondary School certificate (date of birth proof)
  • Educational qualification certificates relevant to the post applied for (Graduation, Shorthand/Typing certificates, etc.)
  • LMV driving licence and proof of 2 years' driving experience (for Process Server)
  • OBC (Delhi) certificate with Non-Creamy-Layer certificate issued on/after 01.04.2026, where claiming OBC reservation (OBC-Outside-Delhi candidates are treated as UR)
  • EWS Income & Asset Certificate valid for FY 2026-27 (based on FY 2025-26 income), issued on or before 04.11.2026
  • Disability certificate, for PwBD candidates claiming reservation/relaxation (minimum 40% relevant disability required)
  • Discharge certificate/proof of military service, for Ex-Servicemen
  • Recent colour photograph (plain background) and signature, uploaded in the prescribed format
Supporting documents are sought only at the e-dossier stage after shortlisting; scrutiny is carried out by the concerned user department (Delhi District Courts), not DSSSB. Candidates who fail to upload the e-dossier within the given time are not considered further.

Important Conditions

  • Candidates must check their own eligibility (qualification, age, experience, PwBD suitability) for each post/department opted; ineligibility found at e-dossier/document verification leads to rejection for that post code with no reallocation
  • SC/ST/OBC/EWS/ESM/PwBD candidates selected purely on general merit are adjusted against unreserved vacancies, not reserved ones
  • Post/department preferences are exercised at the interview stage, are final and irreversible once confirmed, and cannot be changed later
  • Vacancies may vary (increase/decrease) at the discretion of the indenting department, with no compensation to candidates for such changes
  • Mobile phones, calculators, Bluetooth devices, smartwatches, and other electronic gadgets are strictly banned in the exam hall; possession leads to debarment and possible legal action
  • A prescribed dress code applies: light clothing with half sleeves, no big buttons/brooch/badge, Salwar/Trouser, and only slippers/low-heeled sandals (no shoes)
  • Only one registration and one application per candidate are allowed; multiple submissions lead to cancellation and debarment
  • In case of discrepancy between English, Hindi, Urdu and Punjabi versions of the advertisement, the English version prevails
  • DSSSB/Delhi District Courts reserve the right to change the examination scheme, cancel/modify the recruitment, or change exam centres at any stage

What Are State PSC Jobs?

State PSC jobs are government recruitment opportunities notified through State Public Service Commissions. These commissions recruit candidates for various posts and services under state government departments according to the rules applicable to each recruitment.

State PSC recruitment is not limited to State Civil Services examinations. Public Service Commissions may also recruit candidates for engineering, medical, teaching, agriculture, legal, scientific, technical, administrative and other departmental posts.

The posts available depend on vacancies reported by the respective state government departments and the recruitment notifications issued by the commission.

Popular Posts Recruited Through State PSCs

State Public Service Commissions recruit candidates for a wide range of government posts. Common recruitment categories may include:

  • State Civil Services
  • Administrative Services
  • Assistant Commissioner
  • Assistant Director
  • Assistant Professor
  • Lecturer
  • Medical Officer
  • Veterinary Officer
  • Assistant Engineer
  • Assistant Executive Engineer
  • Agriculture Officer
  • Food Safety Officer
  • Drug Inspector
  • Scientific Officer
  • Law Officer
  • Labour Officer
  • Revenue-related Posts
  • Technical Officers
  • Departmental Officers

The actual posts available vary by commission and recruitment notification.

PSC Jobs by Group (Group 1, 2, 2A, 4 & Others)

Several State Public Service Commissions including TNPSC, APPSC, and TSPSC classify recruitment into numbered "Groups" based on post seniority, pay scale, and administrative responsibility. Understanding these groups helps candidates identify which exam to prepare for based on their qualification and career goals.

Group Typical Posts Minimum Qualification Selection Stages
Group 1 Deputy Collector, DSP, Assistant Commissioner, District Registrar Bachelor's degree Prelims + Mains + Interview
Group 2 Assistant Section Officer, Tehsildar, Municipal Commissioner (Grade), Block Development Officer Bachelor's degree Prelims + Mains (some states include Interview)
Group 2A Junior Assistant, Bill Collector, Field Surveyor Bachelor's degree Written Exam (Certificate Verification)
Group 3 Various department Grade II/Non-Gazetted posts Varies by post Written Exam
Group 4 Junior Assistant, Typist, Steno-Typist, Bill Collector, Record Clerk, Village Administrative Officer (VAO) SSLC / 10th or 12th pass (varies by post) Single Written Exam (Certificate Verification)

Group numbering, post names, and minimum qualifications vary by state the table above reflects the common pattern used by TNPSC-style classification. Some states use different group labels or don't use numbered groups at all. Always confirm the exact group structure and eligibility on your state PSC's official notification.

Who Should Apply for Group 4?

Group 4 posts are typically entry-level government jobs open to candidates who have completed SSLC (10th) or Higher Secondary (12th), making them one of the most accessible and high-demand categories of PSC recruitment. These posts don't usually require a specific degree, have a single-stage written exam, and see some of the highest applicant volumes of any PSC exam due to the lower qualification bar and large number of annual vacancies.

State PSC Eligibility Criteria

There is no single eligibility rule for all State PSC jobs. Qualification, age limit, experience and other conditions differ depending on the commission and post.

Eligibility Criteria General Guidance
Educational Qualification Depends on the post and may include Diploma, Graduation, Engineering, Medicine, Law, Post Graduation or another prescribed qualification.
Age Limit Minimum and maximum age limits vary by commission and recruitment.
Age Relaxation Relaxation may be available to eligible categories according to the rules applicable to the recruitment.
State / Domicile Conditions State-specific eligibility, reservation, language or residency conditions may apply to certain recruitments.
Experience Some technical, teaching, specialist or senior posts require relevant professional experience.
Number of Attempts Attempt restrictions apply only where specifically prescribed for an examination or recruitment.

Important: Candidates should check the detailed recruitment notification before applying because eligibility conditions differ for every State PSC recruitment.

State PSC Selection Process

The State PSC selection process depends on the commission and the type of post. There is no single selection procedure followed for every PSC recruitment.

Depending on the recruitment, the selection process may include one or more of the following stages:

  • Preliminary Examination
  • Main Examination
  • Written Examination
  • Screening Test
  • Subject-specific Examination
  • Skill Test
  • Physical Test
  • Interview / Personality Test
  • Document Verification
  • Medical Examination

State Civil Services examinations may have Preliminary, Main and Interview stages, while technical, medical, teaching and departmental recruitment may follow a different selection process.

Always check the individual recruitment notification for the exact examination and selection procedure.

How to Apply for State PSC Jobs 2026

The application process differs slightly between commissions, but candidates can generally follow these steps:

  1. Find the required State PSC recruitment from the latest jobs table above.
  2. Open the detailed recruitment page.
  3. Check the post name, vacancies, qualification, age limit, application fee and important dates.
  4. Read the official recruitment notification carefully.
  5. Open the official application website or application link.
  6. Complete registration or One-Time Registration if required by the commission.
  7. Enter the required personal, educational and category details.
  8. Upload the prescribed photograph, signature and supporting documents.
  9. Pay the application fee if applicable.
  10. Review the application before final submission.
  11. Submit the application before the specified last date.
  12. Save or print the submitted application for future reference.

Candidates should submit applications only through the application method specified in the official notification.

State PSC Exam Pattern and Syllabus

There is no common exam pattern or syllabus for all State PSC recruitments.

State Civil Services examinations generally cover broader subjects such as General Studies and state-specific topics, while technical, medical, engineering, teaching and departmental recruitment may focus more heavily on subjects related to the post.

The following can differ between recruitments:

  • Number of papers
  • Objective or descriptive examination
  • Total marks
  • Exam duration
  • Negative marking
  • Minimum qualifying marks
  • Language requirements
  • Subject-specific syllabus
  • Interview or skill test requirements

Candidates should refer to the syllabus and exam pattern issued for the specific State PSC recruitment they are applying for.

State PSC Jobs vs UPSC Jobs

State Public Service Commissions and the Union Public Service Commission conduct different recruitment processes.

State PSC UPSC
Conducts recruitment for posts and services connected with the respective state. Conducts recruitment and examinations for various Union Government and All India Services posts.
Recruitment rules differ from one State PSC to another. Recruitment is conducted under the rules applicable to UPSC examinations and vacancies.
May recruit for State Civil Services, engineering, medical, teaching, technical and departmental posts. Conducts Civil Services Examination and various other recruitment examinations for Union Government posts.

Candidates looking for Union Government recruitment through UPSC can visit the UPSC Jobs page.

PSC vs PCS - What Is the Difference?

PSC stands for Public Service Commission. It refers to the constitutional commission responsible for conducting recruitment for various government posts and services within its jurisdiction.

PCS commonly refers to Provincial Civil Service or State Civil Services posts and examinations.

A State Public Service Commission may conduct a State Civil Services or PCS examination, but it can also conduct recruitment for many other positions such as Medical Officer, Assistant Engineer, Lecturer, Agriculture Officer and departmental posts.

Therefore, State PSC Jobs covers a broader range of recruitment than only PCS or State Civil Services examinations.

How to Choose the Right State PSC Recruitment

Before applying for a State PSC vacancy, candidates should compare the recruitment requirements with their qualification and preferences.

Check the following details:

  • Required educational qualification
  • Age limit
  • Category and reservation conditions
  • State or language requirements, if any
  • Number of vacancies
  • Pay scale or salary
  • Job location
  • Application fee
  • Selection process
  • Examination pattern
  • Application deadline

Apply only after confirming that you meet the eligibility conditions mentioned in the official recruitment notification.

State PSC Recruitment Updates You Should Check

A recruitment notification can sometimes be followed by additional notices from the commission. Candidates should continue checking recruitment updates even after submitting their application.

Important updates may include:

  • Application date extension
  • Correction window

Latest State PSC Notifications - Frequently Asked Questions

What are State PSC Jobs?

State PSC Jobs are government recruitment opportunities notified through State Public Service Commissions for various posts and services under state government departments.

Which State PSC jobs are currently open?

Currently open recruitments are listed in the Latest State PSC Jobs 2026 table at the top of this page. The list is updated when new recruitment notifications and application updates are released.

Where can I find the latest State PSC recruitment notifications?

You can check the latest State PSC recruitment notifications on this page or select your commission from the State-wise PSC Jobs section to find recruitment specific to your state.

What qualification is required for State PSC jobs?

There is no single qualification required for all State PSC jobs. Depending on the post, candidates may need a Diploma, Graduation, Engineering degree, Medical qualification, Law degree, Post Graduation or another specified qualification.

Are all State PSC jobs for graduates?

No. Eligibility depends on the individual recruitment. Many administrative posts require a degree, while technical, professional and departmental posts may have different qualification requirements.

What is the age limit for State PSC jobs?

The minimum and maximum age limits vary according to the commission and post. Candidates should check the age criteria given in the individual recruitment notification.

Is age relaxation available for State PSC recruitment?

Age relaxation may be available to eligible categories according to the rules applicable to the respective recruitment. The exact relaxation should be checked in the official notification.

Is domicile compulsory for State PSC jobs?

Not for every State PSC recruitment. Some vacancies may have state-specific residency, reservation, language or other eligibility requirements. Candidates should check the relevant recruitment rules before applying.

What is the selection process for State PSC jobs?

The selection process varies by post. It may include a Preliminary Examination, Main Examination, written test, screening test, skill test, interview, physical test, document verification or medical examination.

Do all State PSC recruitments have Prelims and Mains?

No. Prelims and Mains are common in some State Civil Services examinations, but many technical, medical, teaching and departmental recruitments follow a different examination or selection process.

How can I apply for State PSC recruitment?

Open the required recruitment from the latest jobs table, read the eligibility and application details, check the official notification and use the official application link provided on the recruitment page.

What is the difference between State PSC and UPSC?

State PSCs conduct recruitment mainly for posts and services connected with their respective states, while UPSC conducts recruitment and examinations for various Union Government and All India Services posts.

Is PSC the same as PCS?

No. PSC means Public Service Commission, while PCS generally refers to Provincial Civil Service or State Civil Services. A State PSC can recruit for PCS as well as many other administrative, technical, medical and departmental posts.

Where can I check State PSC admit cards?

When an admit card is released, the related recruitment page should be updated with the admit card information and official download link. Candidates can also check the OnlyJobs Admit Card section.

Where can I check State PSC results?

State PSC result updates can be checked through the individual recruitment page or the OnlyJobs Results section.

How often is this State PSC Jobs page updated?

The page is updated when new State PSC recruitment notifications, application extensions and other important recruitment updates become available.

What Is a Bharat Sarkari Job?

A Bharat Sarkari Job is any government job opportunity offered across India's central and state government departments - spanning all 28 states and 8 union territories. The term "Bharat" simply emphasises pan-India coverage: a Bharat Sarkari Job notification could originate from a central body like the SSC, UPSC, or Indian Railways, or from a state public service commission recruiting for state-level posts. Regardless of origin, these roles share the defining traits Indian aspirants seek - long-term job security, government pay scales, and statutory retirement benefits.

Sarkari Job vs Private Job

A sarkari job differs from private-sector employment in a few important ways: government positions are governed by service rules that protect against arbitrary termination, salaries follow Pay Commission recommendations rather than market negotiation, and employees are entitled to pension schemes (NPS or OPS depending on recruitment year), medical coverage under CGHS, and fixed working hours. Private jobs, by contrast, often offer higher starting pay in competitive fields but carry less structural job security.

सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 कैसे भरें? (How to Apply Online)

हर साल लाखों उम्मीदवार सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 भरने की प्रक्रिया में गलतियाँ कर बैठते हैं, जिससे उनका आवेदन रद्द हो सकता है। नीचे दी गई सरल प्रक्रिया से आप अपना फॉर्म सही तरीके से भर सकते हैं।

आवेदन की चरणबद्ध प्रक्रिया

  1. संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना (Notification PDF) ध्यान से पढ़ें और अपनी पात्रता जांचें।
  2. वैध ईमेल आईडी और मोबाइल नंबर से पोर्टल पर पंजीकरण (Registration) करें।
  3. व्यक्तिगत विवरण, शैक्षणिक योग्यता, और आवश्यक दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें (फोटो, हस्ताक्षर, प्रमाणपत्र)।
  4. निर्धारित आवेदन शुल्क का ऑनलाइन भुगतान करें और भुगतान की रसीद सुरक्षित रखें।
  5. फॉर्म सबमिट करने से पहले सभी जानकारी की दोबारा जांच करें और फॉर्म का प्रिंटआउट अवश्य लें।

Documents Required for Sarkari Form

Typical documents needed: recent passport-size photograph (as per specified size/format), scanned signature, educational certificates and mark sheets, category certificate (if applicable), and a valid ID proof (Aadhaar/PAN).

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying

  • Submitting a photo or signature that doesn't match the specified pixel/size requirements.
  • Missing the last date due to server load - apply at least 2–3 days before deadline.
  • Entering a name or date of birth that doesn't match your certificates exactly.
  • Forgetting to download and save the final submitted form and payment receipt.

What is the last date for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026?

Where can I apply for Anganwadi jobs online in 2026?

Forest Guard Recruitment 2026 - Latest Vacancies & Eligibility

Forest Guard recruitment is suitable for candidates interested in forest protection, patrolling and field-level government work. Forest Guard vacancies are generally announced by state forest departments or authorized recruitment boards.

What does a Forest Guard do?

A Forest Guard helps protect forest areas, monitor activities, assist with wildlife conservation and report suspected forest offences. Duties can include patrolling assigned forest areas and supporting senior forest officials.

What is the qualification for Forest Guard Recruitment 2026?

Some Forest Guard recruitments require Class 10 or Class 12 qualifications from a recognized board. However, the exact educational requirements depend on the state and recruitment notification.

Candidates should check:

  • Education: Required qualification and recognized board.
  • Age Limit: Minimum and maximum age, including the age-calculation date.
  • Physical Standards: Height, chest measurements or other applicable requirements.
  • Selection Process: Written examination, physical tests or other notified stages.
  • Vacancies: Total and category-wise posts.
  • Application Dates: Registration opening and closing dates.

How can I apply for Forest Guard Vacancy 2026?

Find the Forest Guard recruitment in the vacancy table above, open the detailed notification, confirm eligibility and follow the official application instructions.

Candidates should apply only through the website or submission method prescribed by the recruiting authority.

Forest Range Officer Recruitment 2026 - RFO Jobs

Forest Range Officer Recruitment 2026 provides opportunities for candidates interested in forest administration, conservation and supervisory roles.

A Forest Range Officer, also referred to as a Range Forest Officer or RFO in some recruitment systems, may oversee forest protection activities, supervise field staff and manage responsibilities within an assigned forest range.

What is the qualification for Forest Range Officer recruitment?

Forest Range Officer recruitment generally involves graduate-level eligibility. Some notifications require degrees in specified subjects such as science, agriculture, forestry or other approved disciplines.

The accepted qualifications vary by recruiting organization. A graduation degree alone does not automatically make a candidate eligible for every RFO vacancy.

How are Forest Range Officers selected?

Depending on the recruitment rules, selection may include:

  • Preliminary or main written examinations
  • Physical standards or fitness assessments
  • Interviews, where prescribed
  • Document verification
  • Medical examination

Candidates searching for RFO Vacancy 2026, Forest Ranger Recruitment or Forest Range Service Officer notifications should check the relevant vacancy details for exact eligibility and selection stages.

There is no single national application website for all state Forest Department jobs.

Recruitment may be handled by a state Forest Department, Public Service Commission, staff selection board or another authorized organization.

To locate the correct official website:

  1. Find your preferred vacancy in the recruitment table.
  2. Open its detailed job notification.
  3. Check the name of the recruiting authority.
  4. Open the official notification PDF.
  5. Follow the application link or instructions provided by the recruiting authority.

Forest Department Recruitment 2026 - Frequently Asked Questions

1. Is Forest Department Recruitment 2026 open?

Forest-related vacancies are announced throughout the year by different recruiting organizations. Check the latest vacancy table above for the status of individual recruitments. An advertised post should be considered open only within its confirmed application period.

2. What is the last date for Forest Department Recruitment 2026?

The last date differs for each recruitment. Check the applicable notification's closing date in the table and verify it against the official announcement.

3. How can I apply for Forest Guard Recruitment 2026?

Find an applicable Forest Guard vacancy, review the educational and physical requirements, and follow the official application instructions before the closing date.

4. Can 10th-pass candidates apply for Forest Department jobs?

Some Forest Guard, Forest Watcher and support recruitments may accept Class 10 qualifications. Eligibility depends on the post and recruiting authority.

5. Can 12th-pass candidates apply for Forest Guard vacancies?

Yes, some Forest Guard recruitments accept Class 12 qualifications. Check the specific notification to confirm any subject or additional eligibility requirements.

6. Can graduates apply for Forest Range Officer recruitment?

Graduates may qualify for certain Forest Range Officer vacancies, but some recruitments require degrees in specified disciplines. Candidates must verify the accepted qualifications.

7. Is a physical test required for Forest Guard recruitment?

Many Forest Guard recruitments include physical standards or fitness tests. The exact requirements depend on the recruiting authority.

8. What is the age limit for Forest Guard recruitment?

The age limit varies by state and notification. Check the official minimum and maximum ages, cut-off date and applicable relaxations.

9. Is there an exam for Forest Department jobs?

Many Forest Guard, Forester and officer-level recruitments include written examinations. Other roles may use different selection methods. Follow the official selection process for the chosen vacancy.

10. What is the difference between a Forest Guard and a Forest Range Officer?

A Forest Guard generally performs field-level protection and monitoring duties. A Forest Range Officer usually carries supervisory and administrative responsibilities for a forest range. Exact duties differ under the relevant service rules.

11. Can ex-servicemen apply for Forest Department recruitment?

Eligible ex-servicemen can apply for vacancies where they meet the recruitment requirements. Reservation benefits and relaxations depend on the applicable rules.

12. Are Forest Department jobs available in every state?

Different states announce vacancies at different times. Not every state or post necessarily has an active recruitment notification at any given moment.

13. Is there a single apply online link for all Forest Department vacancies?

No. Each recruiting organization may use a different application portal or offline application process.

14. Where can I download the official Forest Department notification PDF?

Open the relevant recruitment from the latest vacancy table and follow its official notification link.

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks
Experienced - no exam, interview-based Officer, manager, specialist, medical Professionals with relevant work experience Shortlisting based on qualification/experience, followed by a personal interview

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

Govt Jobs for Law Graduates - Eligibility (LLB, LLM, BL)

Eligibility varies by post, but the core requirement for almost every government law job is a recognised law degree. Senior and specialised roles add experience, an LLM, or Bar enrolment on top.

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor of Law (BL) / LLB (Legum Baccalaureus): the baseline qualification for most legal and law officer posts.
  • LLM (Master of Laws): required for senior legal officer, faculty, and some advisory positions.
  • Integrated 5-year degrees - BA LLB, BBA LLB, BCom LLB - are accepted wherever an LLB is required.

The degree must be from a university recognised by the Bar Council of India.

Bar Council Enrolment & AIBE

For litigation, prosecutor, and standing-counsel roles you generally need to be enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council, and many positions ask for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) Certificate of Practice issued by the Bar Council of India. Purely advisory or research posts (Law Clerk, Research Fellow, Legal Consultant) often do not require enrolment.

Age Limit & Relaxations

The upper age limit is typically 30 to 40 years for the general category, depending on the post and recruiter. Statutory relaxations apply: usually 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and additional relaxation for PwD and ex-servicemen candidates. Always confirm the exact limit and cut-off date in the official notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Salary & Pay Scale for Government Law Jobs

Pay depends on the organisation and grade. Officer-level legal posts under the 7th Pay Commission generally fall in Pay Levels 10 to 12, with a monthly salary roughly between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500, plus Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and other benefits. PSU legal officers are paid on IDA scales, which can be higher at entry grade.

Legal Officer (PSU/Bank, IDA) E1 / Scale I ₹50,000 - ₹1,60,000

Types of Law Officer / Legal Posts in Government Sector

  • Judicial Services - Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional District Judge, High Court Judge, recruited via State Judicial Service Exams (PCS-J)
  • Law Officer / Legal Officer - Roles in public sector banks (IBPS SO Law), insurance companies (LIC AAO Legal), regulatory bodies (SEBI Grade A Legal), and PSUs (Coal India, NTPC, GAIL Legal)
  • Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor - Administrative legal support roles in ministries, universities, and district courts
  • Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO) - Prosecution roles recruited through State PSCs, requiring LLB and often a minimum years of practice

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, ADJ, High Court Judge)

Judicial Services is the most prestigious and highest-paying career path for LLB graduates. Recruitment happens through State Public Service Commissions (e.g., RPSC, UPPSC, MPPSC) via a three-stage exam: Preliminary, Mains, and Interview. Civil Judge posts typically require 0-3 years of practice depending on the state, while some states allow fresh LLB graduates to apply directly.

Law Officer / Legal Officer (Banks, PSU, Insurance)

Public sector banks and insurance companies recruit Law Officers through specialist officer (SO) exams. These posts require only an LLB degree (AIBE not mandatory) and offer competitive pay scales under the 7th Pay Commission equivalent structure, along with allowances.

Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor Posts

These are typically Group B/C administrative-legal posts in ministries, universities, and PSU legal departments, requiring an LLB degree and sometimes relevant drafting/litigation experience.

Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO)

APO recruitment is conducted by State PSCs (e.g., RPSC Assistant Prosecution Officer) and requires an LLB degree, enrollment as an advocate, and in most states, a minimum period of practice (often 3 years).

Selection Process for Law Govt Jobs

The selection process differs by post but commonly includes:

  1. Written examination - testing legal knowledge, aptitude, and general awareness (for judicial services and most exam-based posts).
  2. Interview / viva-voce - assessing legal reasoning and suitability.

Law Govt Jobs FAQ's

What are the latest law govt jobs in 2026?

Current law government jobs in 2026 include Law Officer, Legal Officer, Assistant Prosecution Officer, Judicial Service, and Legal Adviser posts across High Courts, PSUs, public sector banks, and central/state departments. The table above is updated daily with vacancy count, last date, and the official notification link.

Which departments hire LLB and law graduates?

High Courts and District Courts, the Ministry of Law and Justice, UPSC, State Public Service Commissions, public sector banks, PSUs, insurance companies, and regulatory bodies regularly recruit law graduates for legal and judicial roles.

What is the eligibility for government law jobs?

Most posts require a Bachelor of Law (LLB/BL) from a recognised university; senior roles may require LLM and experience. Litigation and prosecutor posts usually require enrolment with a State Bar Council and, often, the AIBE certificate.

What is the salary of a Law Officer in the government sector?

A government Law Officer or Legal Officer typically earns between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500 per month under the 7th Pay Commission, depending on the organisation, plus DA, HRA, and allowances. PSU legal officers draw IDA-scale pay.

Can a fresher LLB graduate get a government job?

Yes. Freshers can apply for Civil Judge (Junior Division) judicial-service exams, Law Clerk and Research Fellow posts in High Courts, and trainee legal roles. Some PSU and bank Law Officer posts require a few years of post-enrolment experience.

How can I apply for law officer vacancies in central government?

Open the post in the table above, read the official notification, register on the recruiter's portal, fill in the application with your LLB and enrolment details, pay the fee, and submit before the last date.

What is the difference between Judicial Services and Law Officer posts

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, via state judiciary exams) places you on the bench as a judge. Law Officer/Legal Officer posts are departmental legal-counsel roles in PSUs, banks, and ministries - advisory and litigation support, recruited by interview or written test.

Is there an age limit for govt law jobs?

Most posts set the upper age at 30 to 40 years for the general category, with statutory relaxations for OBC, SC/ST, and PwD candidates. Check each notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

About DA&FW Senior Agricultural Engineer

The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare functions under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare from Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi. The Senior Agricultural Engineer posts are at its Farm Machinery Training and Testing Institutes: the Central Farm Machinery Training and Testing Institute at Budni (Madhya Pradesh) and the Northern Region, Southern Region and North Eastern Region institutes at Hisar (Haryana), Anantapur (Andhra Pradesh) and Biswanath Chariali (Assam).

Where and How to Send

The application must be routed through proper channel and sent directly to this address:

Under Secretary (M&T), Room No. 12A, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Krishi Bhawan, Dr. Rajendra Prasad Road, New Delhi -110001

  1. Fill the Bio-data/Curriculum Vitae Proforma (Annexure-II) in triplicate. The proforma may be downloaded from www.agriwelfare.gov.in or from the Farm Machinery Training and Testing Institute websites cfmtti.dacnet.nic.in, nrfmtti.dacnet.nic.in, srfmtti.dacnet.nic.in and nerfmtti.dacnet.nic.in.
  2. In item 17 of the proforma, state whether you are applying for deputation (including Short Term Contract), Absorption or Re-employment, and sign the declaration on qualification and work experience.
  3. Sign the Declaration by Applicant (Annexure-IV).
  4. Get the Certification by the Employer/Cadre Controlling Authority (Annexure-III) completed, countersigned and sealed.
  5. Attach the documents listed under Enclosures below.
  6. Submit the application to your employer, which forwards it through proper channel to the Under Secretary (M&T) so that it reaches within 60 days of publication of the advertisement in the Employment News.

The notice does not mention a postal mode or any text to write on the envelope. Advance copies of applications, applications received after the closing date and applications not accompanied by the required certificates/documents are liable to be rejected.

Posts, Eligibility and Pay

There are two posts of Senior Agricultural Engineer, classified as General Central Service, Group 'A' Gazetted, Non-Ministerial, in Pay Level - 11 (Rs. 67700-208700) in pay matrix. The number of vacancies is tentative and may be decreased or increased at the discretion of the Competent Authority.

Who Can Apply

Officers under the Central Government or State Governments or Union Territory administrations or public sector undertakings or agricultural universities or recognised research institutions or councils or semi-government or autonomous bodies or statutory organisations who are:

  • (i) holding analogous posts on regular basis in the parent cadre or department; or
  • (ii) with five years' service in the level rendered after appointment thereto on a regular basis in posts in Level -10 (Rs. 56100-177500) in the pay matrix or equivalent in the parent cadre or department; or
  • (iii) with seven years' service in the level rendered after appointment thereto on a regular basis in posts in Level -7 (Rs. 44900-142400) in the pay matrix or equivalent in the parent cadre or department;

and who possess the educational qualification and experience below.

Essential Qualification and Experience

  • Degree in Agricultural Engineering or Mechanical Engineering from a recognised University or Institute; and
  • Five years' experience in operation and maintenance of tractors, agricultural machinery and allied equipment's including teaching experience in any Government or private listed organisation; or five years' experience in handling independently testing and evaluation of farm machinery and agricultural implements in any Government or private listed organisation.

Desirable

  • Post Graduate Degree in Agricultural Engineering from a recognised University or Institute.

Age Limit

The maximum age limit for appointment by deputation (including short term contract) shall not be exceeding 56 years as on the closing date of receipt of applications. The notice prints no age relaxation.

Who Is Not Eligible

  • Departmental Officers in the feeder category who are in direct line of promotion will not be eligible for consideration for appointment on deputation.
  • Deputationists shall not be eligible for consideration for appointment by promotion.

Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions of the post.

Enclosures

  • Curriculum vitae (in triplicate) in the Annexure-II proforma.
  • Attested photocopies of Annual Performance Appraisal Reports for the last five years, attested by an officer not below the rank of Under Secretary (Annexure-III also allows the CR Dossier in original).
  • Vigilance Clearance/Integrity Certificate/Cadre Clearance Certificate.
  • Statement giving details of major or minor penalties imposed on the officer, if any, during the last 10 years (Annexure-III).
  • Declaration by Applicant (Annexure-IV).
  • Latest salary slip showing basic pay, Dearness Pay/Interim relief/other allowances and total emoluments, when the applicant's organisation does not follow Central Government pay scales.
  • A separate sheet, authenticated by signature, if the space for employment details or additional information is insufficient.

Terms of Deputation

  • The deputation will be initially for a period of one year, but is extendable as per DoPT's guidelines.
  • The period of deputation will include deputation in another ex-cadre post held immediately before this appointment in the same or some other organisation or department in the Central Government.
  • The appointment will not give the appointee on deputation any claim for regular appointment.
  • The deputation is subject to DoP&T circulars, especially the terms in DoP&T's OM No. 6/8/2009 Estt. (Pay II) dated 17.06.2010 and its subsequent amendments.
  • Place of posting can be the Farm Machinery Training and Testing Institute at Budni (Madhya Pradesh) or Hisar (Haryana) or Anantapur (Andhra Pradesh) or Biswanath Chariali (Assam) or the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (Hqrs).

The notice was issued from its office at Shikhar, Plot No. 1, Sector – 29, Gurgaon – 122001. This recruitment is for professionals on a contract lumpsum basis in the Southern region.

All 31 Senior Technical Assistant posts are listed under VC No. CL/12/26 for posting in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry & Lakshadweep.   • General/EWS candidates, and SC/ST/OBC(NCL)/PWD candidates applying against unreserved posts, need a minimum of 50% marks in the minimum educational qualification.
  • Reserved category candidates (SC/ST/OBC(NCL)/PWD, as applicable) need at least 45% marks for consideration against reserved posts. The same applies to candidates with higher qualifications in the same discipline.
  • Candidates with higher qualifications (Degree / PG Degree) in the same discipline are also eligible to apply.
  • The diploma or degree must come from an institution recognised by BTE/AICTE respectively, a university incorporated by a Central or State Act, an institution established by an Act of Parliament, or a university deemed under Section 3 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956.
  • Sections A & B of the Institution of Engineers (India) examination are also accepted.
  • If a mark sheet does not show the percentage, the candidate must provide the university's conversion formula. If the university has none, an undertaking signed by its authorised representative is required, and a minimum of 5 on a 10-point scale is treated as 50%.
  • Training (except on-the-job training), internship, teaching, academic, fellowship or PhD research experience is not counted as experience.
  • The date of acquiring the qualification is the earliest of the following: the last day of the month of the final examination, the date of the result, the date of the final mark sheet, or the date of the degree. No relaxation is given on this point.

Only candidates with not less than 40% of the relevant disability get PWD benefits. The post is identified for locomotor disability (OA, OL) and hearing impairment (HI). Physical requirements include sitting, standing, bending, walking, seeing, manipulation by fingers, communication, and reading and writing. Persons with these disabilities may apply even where no vacancy is reserved for them; they are then considered by the general standard of merit. The relaxations are given subject to the required certificates. For the discipline-specific eligibility of the post, candidates should check the official notification.

How to Apply for RITES Senior Technical Assistant

  1. Open the registration format in the Career Section of the RITES website, http://www.rites.com, between 02.11.2026 and 22.11.2026.
  2. Note the Registration No. that the system generates on top of the form. Quote it in all further communication with RITES.
  3. Fill in the details under "Fill/ Modify Application Form", entering the "Identity Proof" details carefully. The same identity proof must be produced in original at later stages.
  4. Give two preferences for the written test centre.
  5. Upload all documents under the "Upload Document" section.
  6. Pay the fee online under the "Make Payment" section, then download the final application form.
  7. Print, sign and keep a copy of the application form, and carry it if called for selection.

  • The fee paid by SC / ST / PwD candidates is refunded once they take part in the written exam / interview (as applicable). The refund goes to the source account or card, less GST / bank charges, after the category certificate is checked.

Selection and Interview

The RITES Senior Technical Assistant selection consists of a written test followed by document scrutiny. Appointment also depends on medical fitness.

Written Test

The written test has 125 objective type questions of one mark each, with a duration of 2.5 hours. There is no negative marking. PwBD candidates get a compensatory time of 50 minutes. To be considered further, candidates need a minimum of 50% marks (UR/EWS) or 45% marks (SC/ST/OBC (NCL)/PwBD against reserved posts).

Logical Reasoningaround 35Puzzles, seating arrangement, inequalities, Venn diagrams, blood relations, directions, ranking, verbal and spatial reasoning, patterns
Basic Awareness/ General Knowledgearound 20Current affairs; static GK (history, geography, polity, economy, culture, general science)

The tentative test centres are Chennai, Bangalore, Thiruvananthapuram and Secunderabad. RITES may allot a centre that the candidate did not choose. The exact date, time and venue will be communicated separately.

Document Scrutiny and Merit List

Based on the written test result and the number of vacancies, RITES scrutinises the uploaded documents. A merit list is prepared only for candidates who meet the minimum marks and are shortlisted in the document scrutiny. Offers are then issued provisionally. Original documents are verified at joining, and the offer is cancelled if they cannot be verified. Depending on requirement, the written test, document verification or interview may be held at RITES' Regional Offices. Selected candidates must be found medically fit as per RITES Rules.

Indian Army TES 57 Recruitment 2026: The Indian Army has invited online applications for 90 provisional vacancies under the 10+2 Technical Entry Scheme (TES-57), with training scheduled to begin in July 2027. This entry offers unmarried male candidates who have passed Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics an opportunity to become commissioned Army officers. Candidates must have secured at least 60% aggregate marks in PCM and appeared in JEE Main 2026. Online applications are open from 14 October to 12 November 2026, closing at 12:00 noon.

Unlike a regular soldier recruitment, Indian Army TES 57 provides a four-year military and engineering training programme leading to a Permanent Commission in the rank of Lieutenant. Eligible applicants must have been born between 1 January 2008 and 1 January 2011, both dates inclusive. Shortlisting is based on JEE Main 2026 Common Rank List (CRL), followed by a five-day SSB interview and medical examination. Candidates receive a stipend of Rs. 56,100 per month during the IMA training phase only, followed by Level 10 officer pay after successful commissioning.

Download Indian Army TES 57 Recruitment 2026 Notification PDF

Indian Army TES 57 Recruitment 2026 Overview

The following table covers the vacancy, eligibility, age, dates, selection process, training, stipend and commissioning details.

Indian Army TES 57 Vacancy 2026

The Indian Army has announced 90 provisional vacancies for the 10+2 Technical Entry Scheme - 57. Selected candidates will undergo engineering and military training before being considered for Permanent Commission in the Army.

Indian Army TES 57 Eligibility Criteria 2026

Candidates applying for Indian Army TES 57 Recruitment 2026 must have passed Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, secured at least 60% aggregate marks in these three subjects and appeared in JEE Main 2026. The entry is open to unmarried male candidates who satisfy the prescribed nationality, age and medical standards.

Indian Army TES 57 Educational Qualification

  • Must have passed Class 12 or an equivalent examination from a recognized education board.
  • Must have studied Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (PCM).
  • Must have secured a minimum aggregate of 60% marks in PCM.
  • The PCM percentage is calculated using Class 12 marks in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics.
  • Must have appeared in JEE Main 2026.

Is JEE Main 2026 Mandatory for Indian Army TES 57?

Yes. Appearing in JEE Main 2026 is mandatory for TES-57. The Indian Army will shortlist eligible applicants using the JEE Main 2026 Common Rank List (CRL). Meeting the Class 12 PCM percentage requirement alone does not guarantee an SSB interview call.

How Are 60% PCM Marks Calculated for Indian Army TES 57?

The 60% requirement applies to the aggregate marks obtained in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics in Class 12. Candidates must enter their actual PCM percentage up to two decimal places without rounding it off.

Indian Army TES 57 Nationality Requirements

The notification allows unmarried male candidates who satisfy the prescribed nationality requirements, including:

  • Citizens of India.
  • Subjects of Nepal.
  • Eligible persons of Indian origin who migrated from the countries listed in the notification with the intention of permanently settling in India.

Certain candidates require a Government of India eligibility certificate. The notification provides an exemption from this certificate requirement for Gorkha subjects of Nepal.

Indian Army TES 57 Marital Status Requirement

The entry is restricted to unmarried male candidates. Selected candidates must undertake not to marry until they complete the training programme.

A candidate who marries after applying will not be selected for training, even if successful in the selection process. Marriage during training can lead to discharge and recovery of the prescribed training expenditure.

Indian Army TES 57 Age Limit 2026

The age limit for Indian Army TES 57 Recruitment 2026 is 16 years 6 months to 19 years 6 months as on 1 July 2027. Candidates must have been born between 1 January 2008 and 1 January 2011, with both dates included.

Indian Army TES 57 Selection Process 2026

Selection for Indian Army TES 57 begins with shortlisting based on JEE Main 2026 CRL, followed by the Services Selection Board (SSB) interview, medical examination and final merit list. The final merit list is based on SSB marks, subject to medical fitness, eligibility and vacancy availability.

  1. Application Shortlisting: The Indian Army will shortlist applicants based on JEE Main 2026 Common Rank List and the prescribed cut-off.
  2. SSB Interview: Shortlisted candidates will undergo a five-day SSB assessment.
  3. Medical Examination: Candidates recommended by the SSB will undergo a medical examination at a military hospital.
  4. Final Merit List: Merit will be prepared based on marks obtained in the SSB interview.
  5. Joining Letter: Medically fit candidates will receive joining instructions according to merit, eligibility and available vacancies.

Indian Army TES 57 SSB Interview 2027

The TES-57 SSB interviews are tentatively expected between February and March 2027. The SSB assessment is conducted over five days and consists of two stages. Candidates who do not clear Stage I are sent back on the same day.

The SSB assessment includes evaluation by psychologists, Group Testing Officers and Interviewing Officers.

How Is the Indian Army TES 57 Final Merit List Prepared?

The TES-57 final merit list is prepared on the basis of SSB marks. Higher academic qualifications, previous performance and NCC background do not provide additional merit-list weightage. Final joining depends on medical fitness, the candidate's merit position, fulfillment of eligibility conditions and available vacancies.

Indian Army TES 57 Training Period 2027

Selected candidates will undergo four years of integrated military and engineering training. The programme consists of three years at a Cadets Training Wing and one year at the Indian Military Academy, Dehradun.

Indian Army TES-57 cadets receive a stipend of Rs. 56,100 per month during their training at the Indian Military Academy after completing the initial three years of training. On successful commissioning as a Lieutenant, they become eligible for the Level 10 pay scale of Rs. 56,100–1,77,500 and applicable allowances.

How to Apply Online for Indian Army TES 57 Recruitment 2026

Eligible candidates must apply online through the official Indian Army recruitment portal between 14 October and 12 November 2026. The application window closes at 12:00 noon on the last date.

  3. Read the TES-57 notification and application instructions carefully.
  4. Complete the online application with the required personal and educational details.
  5. Enter the correct date of birth as recorded in the accepted Class 10 certificate.
  6. Enter the actual Class 12 PCM aggregate percentage up to two decimal places without rounding off.
  7. Provide the required JEE Main 2026 application details.
  8. Review all entries and submit the application before the closing deadline.
  9. Retain the submitted application details for further recruitment stages.
  10. After the application window closes, download and print the system-generated application form as instructed.

Important: Candidates should submit only one application. Multiple applications by the same candidate may result in cancellation of candidature.

Indian Army TES 57 Application Correction and Printout Instructions

The Army permits candidates to correct application details before the online application window closes. After the final submission process, changes are not permitted under the notification's instructions.

  • Check and correct all application entries before the deadline.
  • Resubmit the application after making permitted changes.
  • The application printout becomes available approximately 30 minutes after the application window closes.
  • Print two copies of the application form carrying the system-generated roll number.
  • Carry one self-attested copy to the SSB interview and retain the other for personal reference.
  • Do not send a hard copy of the application to the Directorate General of Recruiting.

About NaBFID

The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) has been set up under an Act of Parliament, the NaBFID Act, 2021, as the principal entity for infrastructure financing in the country. It is regulated and supervised as an All-India Financial Institution (AIFI) by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). According to the notice, NaBFID supports infrastructure funding by developing innovative financing instruments, bond and derivatives markets, and data-driven risk management.

Where and How to Send

NaBFID accepts applications for this post only by email. The notice states that no other mode of application will be accepted and hard copies are not to be sent.

  1. Visit the link given against the job position for the detailed role description.
  2. Prepare your CV, including a passport sized photograph.
  3. Send the CV by email to [email protected].
  4. Write the subject line strictly as "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF <Job Code>". The job code printed for this post is NABFID/EVP/16.
  5. Make sure the email is received on or before 24 November 2026 by 06:00 pm IST.

Candidates should have a valid email ID and keep it active till the declaration of result, as call letters and interview advice will be sent by email.

Posts, Eligibility and Pay

The advertisement covers a single post in the grade of Executive Vice President: Sl. No. 01, EVP & Head- Market Risk, ALM & Enterprise Risk, Job Code NABFID/EVP/16, 1 vacancy (UR).

Educational Qualification

  • Graduate /Postgraduate in any discipline from a recognized University / Institution or a Chartered Account.
  • Preferred: Certification in Financial Risk Management from Global Association of Risk Professionals (GARP) OR Professional Risk Management Certification from PRIMA Institute.

Experience

  • Minimum 20 years of experience in financial sector.
  • Of these, 5 years should be in risk management function (in RBI regulated entity).
  • Of these 5 years, 2 years should be at senior management level.
  • Experience in the infrastructure domain will be preferred.

Age Limit

The age limit is 55 years and below, as on the date of advertisement. After applying all relaxations in terms of age, the maximum age of candidates shall not exceed 55 years. Candidates should satisfy themselves about their eligibility as on the cut-off date, 3 November 2026.

Nationality

The notice invites applications from Indian Citizens.

Pay and Terms of Engagement

  • Remuneration will be offered based on qualifications, experience, suitability, last drawn salary and market benchmark, and shall not be a limiting factor for suitable candidates. No fixed amount is printed in the notice.
  • Contractual engagement will be for a period of 5 years, which may be renewed for additional terms at the discretion of the Bank.
  • Location of position: Mumbai. Selected candidates may be posted in the Bank's establishment in Mumbai/New Delhi/Anywhere in India, as per the Bank's discretion and requirement.
  • Engagement of the selected candidate is subject to being declared medically fit as per the requirement of the Bank.

Candidates should check the detailed role description linked in the official notification for the full eligibility of the post.

NaBFID Recruitment 2026 Job Description

  • Responsible for developing and implementing NaBFID's enterprise-wide risk framework.
  • Ensuring that the Bank's portfolio is built within the defined risk parameters.
  • Building appropriate mechanisms to measure risk.
  • Providing advice and structuring risk mitigation into the business operations at NaBFID.

A detailed role description is available as a separate document on the NaBFID website, linked from the notice.

Enclosures

  • CV including a passport sized photograph (with the email application).
  • No Objection Certificate from the employer at the time of interview, for candidates serving in Govt./Quasi Govt. offices, Public Sector undertakings including Nationalised Banks and Financial Institutions.
  • Details of criminal case(s) pending, if any, at the time of interview.
  • Proper relieving letters from the employer at the time of taking up the appointment, in case of selection.

Selection Process

Applications will be screened and shortlisted on the basis of eligibility and relevant experience, and the requisite number of shortlisted candidates will be called for interview.

  • Screening and shortlisting: based on eligibility and relevant experience. Merely satisfying the eligibility norms does not entitle a candidate to be called for interview.
  • Additional assessment: shortlisted candidates may undergo psychometric tests and/or assessment centre and/or any other selection method deemed suitable by NaBFID, in addition to the personal interview.
  • Personal Interview: conducted by a committee constituted for this purpose.
  • Final selection: made on the basis of eligibility, experience, qualification and performance during the Personal Interview. Selection is solely at the discretion of NaBFID's Selection Committee, and its decision will be final.

The intimation or call letter for interview will be sent by email or uploaded to the Bank's website. No hard copy of the interview letter will be shared.

  • Government, quasi-government, PSU, nationalised bank and financial institution employees who fail to submit the NOC at interview may not be considered, and travelling expenses otherwise admissible will not be paid.
  • Intimations will be sent by email only to the email ID and mobile number provided; the Bank is not responsible if they do not reach candidates due to a change in contact details, technical fault or otherwise.
  • The Bank may conduct independent verification, including police records, and reserves the right to deny the engagement depending on such disclosures or verification.
  • If a candidate does not fulfil the eligibility norms or has furnished false information or suppressed material facts, the candidature will be cancelled; if detected after appointment, services are liable to be terminated without notice.
  • NaBFID reserves the right to amend, rescind or re-advertise the position at any time without assigning any reasons.
  • Decisions of the Bank on eligibility, interviews, other tests and selection are final; no representation or correspondence will be entertained.
  • Any legal proceedings can be instituted only in Mumbai, and courts, tribunals and forums at Mumbai have sole and exclusive jurisdiction.
  • All changes, updates and corrigenda will be hosted only on the careers page of the Bank's website (nabfid.org/careers); no separate intimation will be issued.

About SBI Risk Specialist Recruitment

The Central Recruitment & Promotion Department of the State Bank of India, located at the Corporate Centre in Mumbai, conducts regular recruitment for specialist cadre officers. This recruitment cycle invites applications for the Risk Specialist position under Middle Management Grade Scale-II (MMGS-II) to handle expected credit loss modelling, macroeconomic overlays, and model risk management.

Vacancy Details

The recruitment offers a total of 3 regular vacancies for the Risk Specialist post under the Unreserved (UR) category (with PwBD-VI horizontal reservation of 1 vacancy). The post-wise and category-wise break-up is detailed below.

Name of Post Type of Vacancy Grade SC ST OBC EWS UR Total
Risk Specialist Regular MMGS-II - - - - 3 3

Who Can Apply

Candidates must fulfill the mandatory educational qualification, age limits, and post-qualification experience requirements as on 31.10.2026.

  • Age Limit: Minimum 25 years and Maximum 35 years as on 31.10.2026. Upper age limit is for unreserved category candidates. Relaxation in upper age limit is available to reserved category candidates as per Govt. of India guidelines (wherever applicable).
  • Essential Qualification: Mandatory: (i) CA or (ii) CFA or (iii) MBA / PGDM or equivalent degree in Finance / Data Analytics / Business Analytics from a recognized institute.
  • Preferred Qualification / Certification: Financial Risk Manager (FRM) by GARP OR Professional Risk Managers by PRMIA (valid as on 31.10.2026).
  • Work Experience: Minimum 2 years of post-qualification work experience in dealing with Expected Credit Loss (ECL) related modelling in Risk Management Department of any Bank / Financial Institution / Rating Agency / Brokerage firm or Risk Advisory in Consulting Firm as on 31.10.2026. Training & teaching experience will not be counted for eligibility.

Pay and Tenure

Selected candidates are appointed in Middle Management Grade Scale-II (MMGS-II) on a regular basis with a basic pay scale of 64820-2340/1-67160-2680/10-93960. The official will be eligible for DA, HRA, CCA, Provident Fund, Contributory Pension Fund i.e. NPS, Leave Fare Concession (LFC), Medical Facility, other perquisites etc. as per Bank’s salary structure.

SBI Risk Specialist Job Description

Selected candidates will be assigned roles and Key Responsibility Areas (KRAs) that include:

  • Development of Probability of Default (PD), Loss Given Default (LGD) and Exposure at Default (EAD) models for various loan portfolio and investments on which ECL is applicable.
  • Development of Macroeconomic Overlays models required as per regulatory guidelines.
  • Implementation of PD, LGD and EAD Models in OFSAA.
  • Period Monitoring, Maintenance and validation of above models.
  • Preparation of Framework for Determination of Stage under ECL.
  • Identification of Significant Increase in Credit Risk (SICR) triggers along with setting qualitative and quantitative triggers for various portfolio.
  • Coordinate with Auditors & Regulator, BUs & other stakeholders throughout model lifecycle.
  • Maintain proper Model documents and database required for audit & regulatory supervision.
  • Develop models required for ECL computation using industry best practices and using statistical and machine learning techniques.

How to Apply for SBI Risk Specialist

  1. Visit the official SBI careers portal at https://sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings.
  2. Navigate to the advertisement for CRPD/SCO/2026-27/27 and click on the registration link.
  3. Register online by providing basic details. Note down the system-generated provisional registration number and password.
  4. Scan and upload your recent passport-size photograph (20 kb - 50 kb, dimensions 200 x 230 pixels) and signature (10 kb - 20 kb, dimensions 140 x 60 pixels) as per the specified dimensions and formats.
  5. Upload required documents in PDF format (not exceeding 500 kb each), including Biodata, Brief Resume, ID Proof, Proof of Date of Birth, Educational Certificates (Relevant Mark-Sheets/ Degree Certificate), Preferred qualification / Certification (if any), Experience certificates, Caste Certificate / EWS Certificate (if applicable), PwBD Certificate (if applicable), and Form-16/Offer Letter/Latest Salary slip from current employer.
  6. Verify all filled details carefully before final submission, as no modifications are allowed after final submission.
  7. Pay the application fee online using Internet Banking, Debit Card, or Credit Card.
  8. Save and print the e-receipt and system-generated online application form for future reference.

Selection and Interview

The selection process consists of two stages:

  • Shortlisting: Mere fulfilling the minimum qualification and experience will not vest any right to candidate for being called for interview. The shortlisting committee constituted by the Bank will decide the shortlisting parameters and thereafter, adequate number of candidates, as decided by the Bank, will be shortlisted for interaction.
  • Interview: Interview will carry 100 marks. The qualifying marks in interview will be decided by the Bank. Merit list for selection will be prepared in descending order on the basis of scores obtained in interview only.

SBI Recruitment 2026 Job Description

Chief Manager (Product & Research - Forex & Rupee Derivatives)

The selected candidate will support the development and delivery of customized solutions to clients. The candidate must also ensure that product offerings stay aligned with evolving market dynamics and regulatory expectations. The job profile includes:

  • Conducting research followed by development of new derivative products in line with the prevailing market.
  • Evaluating the performance of the product on an ongoing basis.
  • Assisting marketing of derivative products to the clients.
  • Providing periodic updates to the Top Management.

Key Responsibility Areas (KRAs):

  • Lead product conceptualization and development of new derivative instruments.
  • Conduct advanced macroeconomic and interest rate research to support product suitability.
  • Prepare product notes, risk disclosures and documentation for approval committees.
  • Evaluate product performance and recommend product positioning strategies.
  • Coordinate with internal departments such as risk, legal, IAD and ITTSS for timely approvals and clearances within the regulatory and internal compliance framework.
  • Coordinate closely with CTMU/RTMUs to drive derivative penetration across the bank's corporate and retail clients.
  • Handle the end-to-end process of product development and approval.
  • Assist in automation and integration of compliance workflows.
  • Mentor AVP-level team members and contribute to strategic product planning.
  • Any other related work as assigned.

Manager (Product & Research Analyst)

  • Design tailored products based on the client's need and market dynamics, and keep up with developments in derivative products and regulatory frameworks.
  • Conduct Fundamental and Technical research across Equities, Forex and Debt Markets.
  • Analyse macroeconomic trends, central bank policies and geopolitical developments, and assess their market impact.
  • Generate and maintain financial models and prepare valuation reports.
  • Monitor the markets and assess the client's requirements.
  • Provide necessary support in product development.
  • Liaise with various departments involved in designing and developing new products.
  • Provide regular updates to the stakeholders and Top Management.
  • Track and analyse corporate earnings, bond yield movements and currency fluctuations.
  • Prepare and present research notes, market outlook and sectoral reports.
  • Collaborate with the trading desk to align strategies with research insights.

For the Manager post, the KRAs may be finalized after selection. The notice states that the job profiles and KRAs for both posts are illustrative, and the bank may assign other roles from time to time.

How to Apply for SBI Recruitment 2026

Applications are accepted only online through the link on the bank's website. No other mode of application will be entertained, and the hard copy of the application and documents must not be sent. Registration is complete only when the fee is paid online on or before the last date.

  1. Log in to https://sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings, scroll down and click on advertisement no. CRPD/SCO/2026-27/26, then download the advertisement.
  2. Click Apply Online and register using a valid email ID and mobile number. Keep both active until the result is declared.
  3. Upload a scanned photograph and signature. The application will not be registered without them.
  4. Fill in the application. Saving it generates a provisional registration number and password, and the saved information can be edited three times only.
  5. Upload each document through its separate Upload link, and check it with Preview. Documents cannot be changed after upload or submission.
  6. Submit the application and pay the fee through the integrated payment gateway (Debit Card/Credit Card/Internet Banking etc.). No edits are allowed after payment, and transaction charges are borne by the candidate.
